question.worked_solution:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

- Start with the graph of $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

- Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\frac{5}{2}.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255908/assets/fcf5bd62bbcaee664ceb36404d3d31d42e726e52c250141a12a9c841563ce039.png)

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is ${y}_{max}=\frac{5}{2}$ and the minimum value is ${y}_{min}=-\frac{5}{2}.$ Therefore, the amplitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude } & =\frac{{y}_{max}-{y}_{min}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{5}{2}-(-\frac{5}{2}))}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{5}{2}+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
